newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * Romania's Foreign Minister Adrian Severin continues his diplomatic mission to the United States to lobby for support for Romania's bid for early admission to NATO.

* The states likely to be on NATO's first eastward expansion have not yet been nominated, said U.S. Department of State spokesman Nicholas Burns. Burns praised Romania for its recent success in implementing refoms and for laying the grounds for a good European partenership.
* The government started its weekly meeting with a debate on banking bills.
* Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea will issue a statement this afternoon on the International Monetary Fund's decision to approve credits totalling $430 million for Romanian reforms.
* Romania's former King Michael visited Norway as part of efforts to win support for the country's NATO integration bid from members of the alliance which are monarchies.
Michael met King Harald of Norway, Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal and Norvegian parliament members.

* President Emil Constantinescu reviewed the 400-strong Romanian troops to be deployed on the Albania peacekeeping mission. He said the mission would help to consolidate Romania's image as a haven of stability in the region.
* Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene will visit Romania starting May 8 to discuss bilateral ties and Romania's bid to join the European Union and NATO.
